challenges.title: Permission Denied
challenges.author: Mehdi Khelifi
challenges.description:
You are `student` on a shared lab machine. The flag is in `/srv/backup/flag.txt` and you are told it is readable — but `cat` says otherwise.

The attached archive contains the directory listing and the lab's setup script.

**Goal:** find the permission mistake and read the file without becoming root.

hints.text: Check the directory permissions, not just the file's.
The backup group has read access to the directory. Are you in it?

challenges.title: Pipe Dreams
challenges.author: Mehdi Khelifi
challenges.description:
A 20,000-line log, one line that matters. You could read it. You should not.

The flag is split across three lines that share a request ID.

**Goal:** find the request ID, then join the three fragments in order.

hints.text: `grep SNT app.log` is a start; the fragments are split, so the brace is not on one line.
Find the `req=` value that appears three times with `fragment=` markers.

challenges.title: Cron Job Snoop
challenges.author: Rania Chaabane
challenges.description:
A web server runs a cleanup script every minute as root. The script lives in a directory the web user can write to.

The archive contains `/etc/crontab`, the script and `ls -la` output.

**Goal:** identify the privilege-escalation path and the flag hidden in the script's backup copy.

hints.text: A root cron job that executes a script from a world-writable directory is a shell waiting to happen.
Check the script's `.bak` — the flag is in the commented-out debug line.

challenges.title: SUID Safari
challenges.author: Mehdi Khelifi
challenges.description:
A deliberately vulnerable container. `find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null` returns one binary that has no business being SUID.

**Goal:** use it to read `/root/flag.txt`. The container image digest and a shell transcript are attached; the challenge is fully local.

hints.text: Compare the SUID list against a clean install of the same image.
It is a standard utility with a documented GTFOBins escape. `-p` preserves the effective UID.

challenges.title: Wildcard Injection
challenges.author: Wael Hammami
challenges.description:
A root cron job runs `tar -czf /backup/site.tgz *` inside a directory owned by the web user. No quotes, no `--`, no `./` prefix.

**Goal:** exploit the wildcard expansion to execute a command as root, then read the flag. Lab container provided as a Dockerfile — build it, break it, document it.

hints.text: Filenames starting with `--` are parsed as options by tar.
